messages.text: Cummins dismisses Khawaja's sandpaper claims as 'utter nonsense'

metadata.summary: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed his former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" after the recently retired batter said in his autobiography that the whole side were aware of ball-tampering that took place on their 2018 tour of South Africa.
metadata.content: Sandpapergate: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismisses Usman Khawaja's claims over ball-tampering scandal as 'utter nonsense' | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sandpapergate: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismisses Usman Khawaja's claims over ball-tampering scandal as 'utter nonsense' Usman Khawaja said in new book 'Sabr' that every Australia player was aware of ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018; current Test captain Pat Cummins, who played in the match, reiterated his denial of involvement and dismissed Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" Friday 13 November 2026 00:11, UK Image: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins held a press conference on Friday that lasted more than an hour Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed his former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" after the recently retired batter said in his autobiography that the whole side were aware of ball-tampering that took place on their 2018 tour of South Africa. Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', which was released earlier this week, bringing the scandal back onto the agenda eight years after Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball while Australia were fielding. Only Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and his vice-captain David Warner were punished, with each receiving lengthy bans as the rest of the Australian team and coaching staff denied knowledge of the scheme. metadata.summary: World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead.
metadata.content: The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content The Annika: Nelly Korda makes impressive return to LPGA Tour action to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots Nelly Korda sits two shots off lead after opening round on return to action; Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin share lead; Lottie Woad and Leona Maguire four shots back; Watch round two of The Annika on LPGA Tour from 4pm on Friday, live on Sky Sports Golf Thursday 12 November 2026 23:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the first round of The ANNIKA Driven by Gainbridge from Pelican Golf Club Belleair World No 1 Nelly Korda made an impressive return to LPGA Tour action after a two-month absence to finish the opening round of The Annika within two shots of the lead. Korda, whose last competitive golf came at the Solheim Cup in September after her most recent LPGA Tour outing in August, shot a bogey-free seven-under par round of 63 at Pelican Golf Club in Florida. Korda trails Japan's Minami Katsu and Korean Hye-Jin Choi by two shots, with fellow American Lindy Duncan also ahead of her on eight under after making a hole-in-one during her 62. metadata.summary: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino have agreed a deal for him to become the club's next head coach.

Pochettino is expected to sign a two-and-half-year contract at Old Trafford, replacing Michael Carrick, who was sacked earlier on Thursday . Pochettino - who had a £7m release clause in his USA contract - will take charge of United after overseeing the USA's games against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday. messages.text: Kane makes history with record 126th England cap

metadata.summary: Harry Kane has broken the record for the most senior England caps by a single player in history.
metadata.content: Harry Kane: England captain breaks Three Lions' appearance record by winning 126th senior cap vs Croatia at Wembley | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harry Kane: England captain breaks Three Lions' appearance record by winning 126th senior cap vs Croatia at Wembley Harry Kane became England's most-capped player with start against Croatia in Nations League; Kane passed Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps; history-making moment comes less than three weeks after the 33-year-old became the first English Ballon d'Or winner for 25 years Thursday 12 November 2026 23:24, UK Harry Kane has broken the record for the most senior England caps by a single player in history. The Three Lions captain led the line for Thursday's Nations League game against Croatia, making his 126th appearance for his country in the process and scoring his 92nd goal to win the game at Wembley . He bypassed the record previously held by goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who earned 125 caps between 1970 and 1990. Shilton paid tribute to Kane on the pitch ahead of kick-off, with Prince William and visiting captain Luka Modric also honouring the England skipper before the game. A stadium-length Tifo was also unveiled in front of the West Stand at Wembley to mark the occasion. The club's first proposal was made in the summer when talks first began over a new contract, but it was turned down by Fernandes. United hold an option to extend the 32-year-old's stay at Old Trafford for a further year and also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January over the possibility of a free transfer.
